Formulation
- Brief summary: Acute eczema flare with marked pruritus causing sleep disruption and impaired concentration; patient has no current regular medications and asthma in past; social context includes flatmates and full-time work; management plan centers on optimized topical therapy, emollients, and an antihistamine with trigger diary and follow-up to assess response.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Relieve itch and rash
  - Improve sleep quality
  - Improve ability to concentrate at work
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Achieve symptom control with prescribed therapy within 7–10 days
  - Establish regular emollient use and maintain a diary of potential triggers
  - Provide effective antihistamine to reduce itch
- Actions (Patient):
  - Use prescribed topical corticosteroid as directed
  - Apply emollients regularly
  - Take antihistamine as advised
  - Track potential triggers in a diary
  - Return for follow-up if symptoms persist or worsen
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Prescribe stronger topical corticosteroid (name not documented)
  - Provide emollients and guidance on bath/shower use
  - Prescribe Fexofenadine (dose/route/frequency not documented)
  - Advise on trigger diary and potential eczema contact dermatitis
  - Schedule follow-up in 1 week; provide patient education

- Not applicable

- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Eczema management with topical steroids, emollients, antihistamines; trigger diary; guidance to monitor improvement and when to return
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Not recorded
- Coping Strategies: Regular skin care with emollients; appropriate use of steroid cream; use of antihistamines as advised; trigger diary
